overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance heavily favors high-concept space and 'What If' planetary scenarios, particularly extreme or counterintuitive planetary conditions (e.g., Venus day vs. year, liquid diamond worlds, dark planets, and supersonic ruby rain). These topics demonstrate significantly higher views-per-day and stronger likes-per-view ratios compared to older psychological or minor biological facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) generated massive traction within short windows.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios involving extreme exoplanets.

winning_patterns.evidence: Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year (970 views) and The Planet Darker Than Coal (1,026 views) outperformed standard animal or brain facts by an order of magnitude.
winning_patterns.action: Use bizarre astronomical contradictions as primary hooks for future space shorts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and song-stuck psychological tricks stagnated below 60-70 views with zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract internal psychology facts unless paired with a high-stakes visual mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated standard animal facts like octopuses having three hearts generated lower velocity in recent runs compared to space anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content strictly toward cinematic survival or extreme prehistoric/deep-sea anomalies rather than basic trivia.
